releases.name: Git That Shit v0.3.0
releases.body:
# Git That Shit v0.3.0

Automatic pre-disaster snapshots for OpenCode AI coding agent config and state files.

> "Oh Shit Git" is what you say after the disaster. Git That Shit is what the tool does *before* the disaster.

Git That Shit is a safety plugin for OpenCode V2 plus a standalone `gts` CLI over the same snapshot
engine. Before risky operations it snapshots fragile config and agent-state files into an isolated
shadow git repository, so one malformed edit, one bad command, or one accidental overwrite stays
recoverable. Inspired by `etckeeper`.

**Verified source commit:** `6069f916a0fac14439c3335e682f994466961851`
**Package:** `@gitdamnit/opencode-git-that-shit@0.3.0`
**Supported OpenCode:** 2.0.x (verified on **2.0.21**, depends on `@opencode/plugin` 2.0.21)
**License:** Apache-2.0

---

## Highlights

- **OpenCode V2 native.** Migrated from the V1 `@opencode-ai/plugin` interface to
  `Plugin.define({ id, setup })`. All eight tools (`gts_status`, `gts_list`, `gts_diff`,
  `gts_restore`, `gts_snapshot`, `gts_prune`, `gts_config`, `gts_doctor`) are registered through
  `ctx.tool.transform` with JSON Schema inputs.
- **Verified snapshots.** A snapshot is only reported as a recovery point when its commit is
  confirmed to resolve in the shadow repository (`git rev-parse --verify <hash>^{commit}`).
- **Real pruning.** `gts prune --yes` rewrites shadow history to keep the newest N snapshots, always
  writing a safety `git bundle` first and moving the branch atomically. Preview remains the default.
- **Independent by design.** Works alone or alongside Checkpoint Orchestrator and Stranger Danger, in
  any load order, with no shared code, state, or initialization.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @gitdamnit/opencode-git-that-shit
```

Then add the plugin to `opencode.json(c)`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@gitdamnit/opencode-git-that-shit"]
}
```

> **npm publication is pending for this version.** Until `0.3.0` is published to npm, `npm install`
> resolves to the latest published version, `0.2.2`. To use `0.3.0` now, build from the source
> archive attached to this release (`npm ci && npm run build`) or from the git tag `v0.3.0`. This
> GitHub release does **not** make `0.3.0` available through npm.

The `gts` CLI works without an active OpenCode session:

```bash
gts version && gts status && gts list && gts snapshot
gts restore <hash>            # dry-run by default
gts restore <hash> --yes      # restore, skipping files changed since the snapshot
gts restore <hash> --yes --force   # overwrite conflicting files
gts prune --keep 20 --yes
```

## Security hardening

- **Secret redaction.** JSON key redaction, YAML/TOML/`.env`/`.jsonc`/shell line redaction,
  `Authorization` headers, multiline PEM blocks. The global OpenCode config is redacted before being
  stored. Files that cannot be processed safely **fail closed** and are skipped, never stored raw.
- **Redacted files are never restored.** A snapshot holds `[REDACTED]` placeholders, not real
  values, so restoring them would destroy live credentials. Restore **skips** redacted files and
  reports them; re-enter secrets manually.
- **Restore is dry-run by default.** Overwriting conflicting files requires `--force`. A
  `pre-restore` recovery snapshot is recorded automatically.
- **Symlink hardening.** Restore refuses symlinked destinations and destinations whose nearest
  existing ancestor resolves outside the project, and writes atomically via an
  `O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` temp file + `rename`.
- **Private storage permissions.** Git That Shit's own storage uses `0700` directories and `0600`
  files (config, manifest, lock, snapshot copies, prune bundles) on POSIX platforms.
- **Project-scoped locking.** Snapshot, restore and prune run under one atomic exclusive lock;
  stale locks are reclaimed only when provably stale.
- **Snapshot-failure safety.** `snapshot.failureMode` adds `standard` (default: continue with a clear
  warning
